entities.summary: The Times is a British newspaper founded in 1785, marking the beginning of a new era in journalism. It played a crucial role in shaping the public's perception of the French Revolution, with its coverage of the Reign of Terror and the rise of Napoleon. The Times' impact extended beyond Britain, as it influenced the way the world reported on politics, society, and culture. The newspaper's commitment to factual reporting and its role in shaping the public's understanding of historical events have made it a cornerstone of modern journalism. As the first daily newspaper to be published in the modern era, The Times has left an indelible mark on the course of human history. The newspaper's influence can be seen in the way it has shaped the way we consume news, and its impact on the development of modern democracy cannot be overstated.
